hook.line: Here are five secret codes for Claude.
hook.visual: Close face to camera with a white pill title 'Secret Codes for Claude' and a flushed emoji; he counts on his fingers, then the title swaps to '#1 /ghost' by 1.9 s

beats.what: Face to camera, white pill title with emoji
Title switches to '#1 /ghost' while he is still on camera
Screen recording of the Claude prompt box on an orange background, red box around the typed code
#2: red box around 'ARTIFACTS' at the end of the prompt
A finished bubble-pop game appears as the result
#3: 'OODA' boxed in red before the prompt; framework diagram in the answer
Zoom punch on the L99 example answer
Cut back to face with '#5 /godmode' title
Face again with pill 'Comment "Codes" and I'll DM you a link'

why_it_works: Numbered list (#1 to #5) with each number in the title pill, so the viewer always knows how far is left
Each code is shown typed in the real product with a red box around it, then the result, so every claim has proof in 2-4 s
Fast pace: 25 cuts per minute and 4.1 words/s with almost no silence (7% measured)
Same formula per item ('just put this before your prompt and...'), so items are easy to follow at speed
weaknesses: Claims like 'passes AI detectors' are unverified and the codes are mostly placebo, which risks trust
Small word captions at the bottom compete with dense UI text in the screen-recording shots
Two CTAs (follow and comment) stacked at the end dilute each other
for_robert: Mark the exact thing to type with a red box on the screen recording and cut to the result within 3 s; Fred could swim to the boxed word and tap it instead of a static box.
